title: Tetranuclear Lanthanide(III) Complexes Containing a Square-Grid Core: Synthesis, Structure, and Magnetism

synthesis.procedure: All complexes 1–4 were prepared by the same procedure. Dy(NO3)3·5H2O (0.13 mmol, 0.057 g) was added to a stirring solution of LH4 (0.041 g, 0.13 mmol) in methanol (10 mL) to give an intense yellow solution. After 15 min of stirring at room temperature, triethylamine (0.051 mL, 0.39 mmol) was added dropwise and the mixture was stirred for a further 12 h at room temperature. The solution was filtered and kept for crystallization; slow evaporation of the mother liquor for about 9 d afforded yellow crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction.
synthesis.time: 15 min then 12 h stirring; crystallization ~9 d
synthesis.vessel_or_method: stirring in methanol; filtration; slow evaporation crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filtered and kept for crystallization; slow evaporation of the mother liquor for about 9 d gave yellow crystals

properties.summary: χMT at 300 K is 56.0 cm3 K mol−1 (expected 56.7 cm3 K mol−1 for four uncoupled Dy3+), decreasing to 43.9 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K, consistent with crystal-field effects and very weak exchange. Magnetization at 2 K and 5 T is 20.9 μB. ac susceptibility shows an out-of-phase χM″ signal below 15 K at zero dc field with a QTM tail; a 3 kOe dc field reduces QTM. Frequency/temperature dependence of χM″ is not typical SMM behavior and is attributed to overlapping contributions from more than one crystallographically independent Dy3+ center; no energy barrier was extracted.

measurements.name: χM″ onset / QTM
measurements.value: χM″ signal below 15 K with QTM tail at Hdc = 0; full ac data at Hdc = 3 kOe (28–1500 Hz, ~2–6 K)
measurements.conditions: ac susceptibility, Quantum Design MPMS 5S SQUID

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the general procedure for 1–4 using Er(NO3)3·5H2O (0.13 mmol; experimental quantities listed as 0.057 g, 0.13 mmol with Et3N 0.051 mL, 0.39 mmol and LH4 0.041 g, 0.13 mmol in methanol). properties.summary: dc magnetic behavior is similar to 1. Magnetization at 2 K and 5 T is 17.5 μB. Only the onset of a χM″ signal is observed above 2 K, even with an applied dc field (Figure S10). Slow relaxation of magnetization at low temperature is noted for the Er derivative, but without a well-defined SMM maximum in the accessible window.
